candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — client rights, legal responsibilities, and safety-related care management
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — restraint orders and client rights
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize federal order limits for violent-behavior restraint: no standing/PRN orders, adult renewal up to 4 hours, and earliest-possible discontinuation.

options.A: Standing or PRN orders are not permitted; for an adult, a violent-behavior restraint order may be renewed for up to 4 hours at a time, subject to reassessment and more restrictive state law.
options.B: A PRN restraint order is acceptable whenever the client has a documented history of violent behavior.
options.C: One restraint order may remain active for 24 hours without renewal if staff continue documenting agitation.
options.D: Once the restraint order is written, the restraint must remain in place for the full ordered period even when the unsafe behavior resolves.

candidate.rationale: Federal hospital rules prohibit standing or PRN restraint/seclusion orders. For violent or self-destructive behavior, renewal limits are age-based; for adults 18 or older, each renewal may be for up to 4 hours. Restraint must be discontinued at the earliest possible time and remains subject to monitoring, reassessment, and applicable state law.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Federal hospital rules prohibit standing/PRN restraint orders, set a 4-hour adult renewal maximum for violent/self-destructive behavior, and require earliest-possible discontinuation.
candidate.source_document_title: 42 CFR §482.13 — Condition of participation: Patient's rights
candidate.stem: A hospital uses restraint for violent or self-destructive behavior in an adult after less restrictive measures are ineffective. Which statement about the order is accurate under the federal hospital Conditions of Participation?
